title: Live playback follow-ups from the #720 final reviews
acceptance: Apple adapter: during a same-song re-cue, a playing state from the previous queue that falls inside atThisCue()'s window no longer counts as this start's evidence, or a real-device run shows that case cannot happen; either way the outcome is recorded.
Apple adapter: when the re-cue setQueue in play() throws, startArmed is cleared at once, with a test.
Live: Next, Previous, Skip track or a Full List row (jumpTo) after a playback error and Retry recover the same way (resume in place or rebuild the coordinator), or the record states why they differ.
Apple adapter: the starting hold kept after destroy() is removed if it has no effect (the runtime builds a new adapter per job), or its purpose is documented.
Live timeline: the strip ignores non-primary mouse buttons (a right-click or middle-click does not start a gesture or seek), with a test. This already happened before #720.
Live: togglePlay cancels the commit throttle before resume or pause, consistent with Retry, jumpTo and Continue without music, or the record states why it need not.
Live: seekRelease reuses seek() for its error and send paths instead of duplicating them.
nextAction: Pick these up after #720 merges and the owner's iPhone Safari run; the first item needs that device run (?playback-timing=1, a timeline re-cue within the same song). Agent-created: Backlog until the owner sets Ready.

evidence.summary: Final review of #720 at 8f12fe9 listed these five as not significant, to be logged as Backlog: same-song re-cue evidence in onPlayingState, startArmed after a setQueue throw, jumpTo resuming in place versus Retry rebuilding, the no-op starting hold after destroy(), and the test-only guardHolders reset. Recorded from the review, not verified.

Final review of #720 at 0f1ea0a (merged as 840255c) found no significant issues. It added three not-significant notes: the strip accepts non-primary mouse buttons (already in production before #720), togglePlay does not cancel the throttle (not reachable as a double start, since every release flushes or cancels), and seekRelease duplicates seek(). The Air conductor checked them against the code.
